Subject: Post-demo recap + initial rerank suggestions

Hi Elena —

Thanks again for walking us through your current search stack this morning. Quick recap and the concrete next steps I promised: 

1) What we heard: ReCommerce is prioritizing higher relevance for product search while keeping median p99 latency under 150ms. You care most about reducing bad results for mid-tail queries and improving CTR on recommended products.

2) Preliminary model recommendations (for evaluation):
- redwood/rerank-base-v2 (8-bit quantized) — good latency/cost balance for inline rerank.
- open/rerank-turbo-1 — stronger on long context but slightly higher token cost.
- fallback: redwood/smaller-bowish-ranker — cheap, lower quality for tail cases.

3) Artifacts attached: promptset_candidate_v3.jsonl (50k human-labeled query-doc pairs), and a starter benchmark (rerank_ndcg_mrr_v1.csv) with synthetic NDCG/MRR baselines we ran on a small holdout. Also included a short canary_playbook outline for rollout.

4) Ask from you: could you share your acceptance criteria (target NDCG@10 or MRR improvement over incumbent) and any hard latency limits for online rerank? If you can, please also indicate whether we can run our evaluation on your anonymized logs or if you prefer we evaluate with the provided promptset.

Next steps I propose:
- You confirm acceptance criteria + whether we can use logs (reply here).
- If yes, we’ll run a 2-week A/B canary plan with Sanity checks + regression alerts; if not, we’ll expand the promptset to better cover your tail.

I’ll loop Marissa (CS lead) and Neha (Solutions) to scope the validation and canary plan once we have the criteria.

Best,
Rishi Malhotra
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference

- Logs: we can provide a 7-day anonymized click log extract (S3 link) but need an NDA addendum before you run anything on our raw logs.

Rishi / Neha — quick internal update after running the validation on the candidate promptset + small log proxy: 

Summary of findings (short):
- redwood/rerank-base-v2: NDCG@10 = 0.72 (incumbent baseline on our holdout: 0.67), MRR = 0.58 vs baseline 0.52. Latency median 38ms, p99 132ms (on our benchmark hardware with similar CPU offload config).
- open/rerank-turbo-1: NDCG@10 = 0.76, MRR = 0.62, latency p99 210ms (exceeds their hard SLA for online rerank without additional engineering).
- fallback candidate: NDCG@10 = 0.60, MRR = 0.46 (cheap but weaker).

Notes:
- The differences shrink when we add emoji-heavy titles and markup; we recommend normalizing product titles (strip HTML, map emoji to tokens) in the evaluation pipeline. I attached rerank_ndcg_mrr_v1.csv with per-query buckets and the promptset_candidate_v3.jsonl we ran.
- Proposed canary plan: 2-week A/B (10% traffic to new model variant), with automated quality regression alerts (NDCG drift > 1.5% absolute) and rollback on any increase in negative engagement (>2% relative). See attached canary_playbook_v0.2.md for details.

Suggested next steps to present to Elena:
1) NDA addendum for log access (legal).
2) Agree to normalization rules for product titles.
3) Run a 7-day evaluation on their anonymized logs (if NDA ok) to get production-aligned baselines.
4) If results look similar to our internal validation, run the 2-week canary with automatic rollback.

I’ll mark follow-ups in the shared Drive folder for transparency.
